accounting.rationale: PDF 63 defines the coarray subject, remote-reference capability and scalar/array admission; the fine units keep the definitional and permission parts separate.
A coarray is a component or variable with nonzero corank. Component rules remain in 7.5.4.3, variable rules in 9.2 and declaration routes in 8.5.6.
Remote reference/definition capability is a coarray concept. Actual image selection, segment ordering and communication semantics remain with 9.6 and 11.7; no single-image fixture is introduced here.
The source admits scalar and array coarray variables. Ordinary rank, array bounds and array-element behavior remain with 5.4.6, 8.5.8 and 9.5.
Limits variable-only coarray requirements to coarray variables rather than type components. This is a scope qualifier for downstream coarray catalogues, not a separate component-value oracle.

Defines corresponding coarrays across the team of establishment, including recursion-depth correspondence. Team/image observations are out of scope for single-image source packets and are owned by coarray/team rules.
Defines the rectangular corresponding-coarray pattern and the terms codimension, corank and cobounds. 8.5.6 and 9.6 own declaration and image-index uses of those terms.
NOTE 1 describes an incomplete final rectangular pattern; notes are not normative requirements.
Records permitted coarray access with cosubscripts and same-image access without them. Image selection and segment-order requirements remain with 9.6 and 11.7.
Defines the subobject predicate that preserves coarray status. Vector subscripts, allocatable/pointer component selection and subobject syntax remain with clauses 7 and 9.
Defines coindexed image-index determination by analogy to array element order. The concrete array element order oracle is owned by 9.5.3.3; coindexed observations need coarray execution support.
Records availability of intrinsic procedures for image-index/cosubscript mapping. The procedures and any exact result relations are owned by their Clause 16 catalogues.
NOTE 2 discusses possible hardware representations and is not normative.
NOTE 3 illustrates same-image cosubscript access and segment-order context; the normative access and ordering rules are p5 and 11.7.

review_rationale: Source registration for 5.4.7-5.4.11 and 5.5-5.5.7 of the Clause 5 overview (batch250). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; restated rules are cross-referenced to their owning catalogues, R516 had no existing tests, and processor-dependent text is latitude. Source accounting only.
